glossary.regime: How the model describes the market now: rising, falling, moving sideways or experiencing unusually large moves.
glossary.probabilityUp: The model's estimate of the chance that the market rises over the selected period.
glossary.volatility: How sharply prices move up and down. Higher volatility usually means greater short-term risk.
glossary.riskState: A composite assessment of current risk based on volatility, drawdown and market state.
glossary.forecastInterval: A range of possible outcomes. A wider range means the model is less certain.
glossary.drawdown: The fall from the most recent peak. A 10% drawdown means the value is 10% below that peak.
glossary.var: Value at Risk (VaR) is an estimated loss threshold under normal conditions. It is not the largest possible loss.
glossary.es: Expected Shortfall is the average loss in cases that are worse than the VaR threshold.
glossary.sharpe: Excess return per unit of total risk. Higher is better.
glossary.sortino: Like Sharpe, but only penalizes downside volatility.
glossary.calmar: Annualized return divided by maximum drawdown.
glossary.profitFactor: Gross profit divided by gross loss. Above 1 means net profitable.
glossary.winRate: The share of trades that were profitable.
glossary.turnover: How actively the portfolio trades. More turnover means more cost.
glossary.exposure: The share of time the system holds a market position.
glossary.basis: The spread between the futures price and the underlying index.
glossary.coverage: The share of actual outcomes that fell inside the forecast range. It shows whether that range was reliable.
glossary.monteCarlo: Monte Carlo simulation creates many possible scenarios to estimate the range of outcomes and risks.
glossary.bootstrap: Repeatedly resampling past data to check whether a result is stable or may have occurred by chance.
glossary.downsideProbability: The estimated probability of a negative return over the evaluation horizon.
glossary.modelConsensus: The degree of agreement between independent models on the current market state.

comparison.title: Higher return than the market, at lower risk
comparison.description: From the start of 2024 to mid 2026, Model Modus achieved a higher increase in capital than {benchmark} while holding a position about a fifth of the time and recording a materially smaller decline. That combination is what merits attention in a rule-based system.
comparison.drawdownNote: Over the same period {benchmark} declined {benchmarkValue}, roughly {ratio} times deeper. This is the loss a holder had to absorb before the portfolio recovered.
comparison.exposureLabel: Share of time holding a position
comparison.exposureNote: For the remaining time the system holds no position and carries none of the market's movement.
comparison.sharpeNote: The Sharpe ratio, measuring return earned per unit of volatility accepted. A value above 1 is generally considered good.
comparison.basisNote: Model Modus trades a leveraged futures contract; {benchmark} is an unleveraged index return. Both lines cover the same period and the same trading days.

performance.title: Test Results
performance.description: Model Modus is Quant Percent's main trading system, running on VN30F1M futures. This page publishes its 2024–2026 test: the model learned only from earlier years and was then tested on the following one, so the result does not depend on knowing the future.
performance.labelNote: Every figure on this page comes from simulation on historical data. These are research results, not live trading, and not a commitment about future performance.
performance.restatementNote: The order-fill simulation was tightened on 4 July 2026 to treat sessions that open beyond a stop level more conservatively. The reports below were produced under the earlier method and are being rerun to the new standard.

system.reportsLead: The result below comes from a single evaluation spanning the whole 2024–2026 period, tested in chronological order.
system.curveCaption: Illustration: capital of a separate run on 2025–2026 data

detail.tradeIndexNote: The horizontal axis is the closed-trade number. The source run records profit per trade without timestamps.
detail.seriesNote: Portfolio value from the middle-ranked run (#{seed}) out of {total} runs; the horizontal axis is the closed-trade number.
detail.foldNote: For each period, the model learns only from earlier data and is then tested on the following year. Periods remain separate to avoid overstating capital growth.

detail.seedDistribution: How much do results change across repeated runs?
detail.seedDistributionNote: The model was run {seeds} times on the same data; {positive} runs ended positive. Trade direction remains unstable: {long} runs lean long and {short} lean short.
detail.bootstrapTitle: Are results stable when the data changes slightly?
detail.bootstrapNote: The recorded profit series was resampled {n} times to estimate how much results could vary.
detail.bootstrapProb: Chance that the profit-to-loss ratio is above 1
detail.costStress: How do trading costs affect the result?
detail.costStressNote: Reference config: {fee} points fee and tax per round trip, {slippage} points slippage per side. The table measures mean profit at different applied cost levels.
detail.ciNote: Estimated by repeatedly resampling the results from all runs.

about.title: About
about.whatText: Quant Percent is a data-driven market research group. We build models to understand market direction, estimate risk and test rule-based trading methods in Vietnam.
about.focusText: We focus on the VN-Index, stocks listed on HOSE and the VN30F1M futures contract. Keeping the scope fixed lets data collection, model building and testing stay consistent.
about.philosophyText: Forecasts are never certain, return always comes with risk, and every model has periods when it works poorly. Every conclusion on this site states where the data came from, which period it was tested on and what its limits are.
about.visionText: To build an asset management organization in Vietnam where decisions are based on data, technology and a clear risk process.
developingItems: Multi-horizon forecasting for indices and stocks
about.note: Quant Percent does not currently operate formal asset management and does not raise or accept capital through this website.
about.lead: We build quantitative tools for the Vietnamese market, and publish what does not work alongside what does. Most quantitative research does not survive contact with new data — we think that is worth saying rather than hiding.
about.stageText:
Quant Percent is in its research and validation phase. Four models have completed independent chronological testing, the data system runs daily across every stock listed on HOSE, and Model Modus has been through three years of validation.

The next step is supervised operation before any increase in scale.
about.publishText:
Every report states the data period, the validation method and a full set of performance and risk metrics. Results are broken out by period, including periods that lost money.

A model version enters use only after clearing independent validation criteria.
about.ctaTitle: Interested in this line of research?
about.ctaText: We speak with institutional investors, data partners and research collaborators.

legal.title: Legal
legal.intro: Please read the following terms carefully before using content on the Quant Percent website.

items.title: Nature of content
items.text: Quant Percent is currently a quantitative research group. Content on this website is provided for informational and research purposes only and does not constitute personalized investment advice, an offer to invest, or any guarantee of returns.

items.title: Forecast uncertainty
items.text: All forecasts carry uncertainty. Forecast intervals and probabilities are statistical estimates, not commitments about outcomes.

items.title: Past results
items.text: Past results, including backtests and paper trading, do not guarantee future outcomes.

items.title: Backtest limitations
items.text: Backtests are built on historical data and may be affected by overfitting, selection bias and execution assumptions.

items.title: Paper trading
items.text: Paper trading is simulated operation and differs from live trading in execution, liquidity, costs and psychology.

items.title: Data delays and revisions
items.text: Displayed data may lag real time and may be revised as data sources update.

items.title: Model changes
items.text: Models are under continuous research and may change, be paused or be removed without notice.

items.title: User responsibility
items.text: Users are solely responsible for their own investment decisions. Trading securities and derivatives carries risk of capital loss.

items.title: No substitute for professional advice
items.text: Information on this website does not replace investment, legal or tax advice from licensed professionals.

legal.reviewNote: This content requires review by qualified legal counsel in Vietnam before the website goes into production.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes how Quant Percent collects, uses and protects your personal data when you use this website.

sections.title: Data we collect
sections.text: When you submit the contact form, we collect your name, email, phone and organization (if provided), inquiry type and message. The current version of the website does not require accounts.

sections.title: How we use it
sections.text: Contact data is used only to respond to your inquiry and, if you registered interest, to inform you about future research and partnership opportunities. We do not sell or share your data with third parties for advertising.

sections.title: Storage and protection
sections.text: Data is stored with access control and processed only by responsible personnel. We apply reasonable technical measures against unauthorized access.

sections.title: Retention
sections.text: Contact data is retained for as long as needed to handle your inquiry and at most 24 months after the last contact, unless the law requires otherwise.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data by contacting us through the website form.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.text: This website uses only technical cookies necessary for operation (such as remembering your language). No advertising or third-party tracking cookies are used.

portfolio.title: Where is your portfolio concentrating risk?
portfolio.description: Enter your holdings and the system measures the portfolio against the price history of those exact stocks: value, profit, volatility, potential loss and, most importantly, which holding contributes most of the risk. Every stock listed on HOSE is supported.
portfolio.scopeNote: This is a measurement tool, not investment advice. It does not recommend buying or selling anything. Every figure is computed from prices that have already happened, except the one block that names the model it came from.

form.heading: Current holdings
form.lead: Enter a ticker and a share count. Every stock listed on HOSE is supported. Cost basis may be left blank when analysing a hypothetical portfolio; the profit columns then remain empty rather than showing inaccurate figures.
form.cashNote: Cash counts towards portfolio value but carries no risk.
form.horizonNote: Used for the forward decline estimate.
form.privacy: Your holdings are not retained. The data is sent for calculation and then discarded, never written to the database and never placed in the page URL.

errors.quantity: The share count for {symbol} is not valid.
errors.empty: At least one stock is needed to analyse.

form.symbolHint: Type a ticker or pick from the suggestions.

errors.notAnalysable: The holdings do not share enough common price history to measure risk. Please remove recently listed or thinly traded stocks.
errors.unknownSymbol: One of the tickers was not found in the data.
errors.contract: The response did not match the expected format.

result.unpriced: {count} ticker(s) lack enough price history and were left out: {symbols}. The figures below cover the rest of the portfolio.
result.noCostBasisNote: a cost basis is needed to compute profit
result.betaAbove: moves about {pct} more than the market
result.betaBelow: moves about {pct} less than the market
result.betaMissing: not enough index data to compare
result.standout: {symbol} represents {weight} of portfolio value but contributes {risk} of total risk, owing to high volatility ({vol} a year) and a tendency to move with the rest of the portfolio.
result.contributionLead: Share of capital reflects the money allocated to each holding. Share of risk reflects that holding's responsibility for the movement of the whole portfolio. The two rarely coincide.
result.diversificationLead: The portfolio holds {positions} stocks, but once co-movement between them is taken into account, its diversification is equivalent to about {bets} independent positions.
result.effectiveBetsNote: after accounting for co-movement between holdings
result.avgCorrelationNote: the closer to 1, the more the holdings move together
result.sectorMissing: no sector data for these tickers
result.closestPair: The most correlated pair is {a} and {b}, at {value}. Holding both is close to doubling a single position.
result.lossHeading: Potential loss the portfolio may absorb
result.lossLead: The figures below are measured on this portfolio's own last {days} sessions (about {months} months). They are recorded results, not forecasts.
result.var95Note: on the worst 5% of sessions, the one-day loss exceeds {amount}
result.es95Note: the average loss across those worst 5% of sessions, about {amount}
result.maxDrawdownNote: measured from the highest point in the period
result.forwardLead: This takes the simulated VN-Index distribution from {origin} ({paths} scenarios) and carries it across to the portfolio using a beta of {beta}.
result.forwardCaveat: This is an indirect estimate: it carries the index's risk across by beta, so it does not capture risk specific to the individual holdings. A simulated probability is not a certainty.
result.provenance: Computed on the {days} sessions every holding traded, taken from the last {lookback} sessions, current to {asOf}. The covariance matrix uses Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage to stay stable when the number of sessions is limited.
result.glossaryLead: Explained using the portfolio just entered.

explain.var95: On average about one session in twenty is adverse. The 95% loss threshold indicates that on such a session the loss is typically {pct} or more, around {amount}. It marks where the adverse range begins, not the maximum loss.
explain.es95: A threshold identifies where the adverse range begins but not how severe it becomes. This figure is the average loss across those adverse sessions: about {pct}, or {amount}.
explain.maxDrawdown: Had this portfolio been held throughout the measured period, its value at one point stood {pct} below the peak previously reached, around {amount}. This is a recorded decline, not an estimate.
explain.downside: Overall volatility ({total}) counts rising and declining sessions alike. The {pct} figure counts declining sessions only, which better reflects the risk that concerns an investor.
explain.riskContribution: Share of capital is the money allocated to a holding. Share of risk is that holding's responsibility for the movement of the whole portfolio, depending both on its own volatility and on how closely it moves with the others. A holding representing a quarter of capital can contribute more than half of total risk.
explain.effectiveBets: The portfolio holds {positions} stocks, but if they move together then in risk terms the diversification achieved is equivalent to fewer holdings. Accounting for this, the portfolio is equivalent to about {bets} independent positions.
explain.beta: A beta of {beta} means that when VN-Index moves 10%, this portfolio typically moves about {move} in the same direction. Above 1 is more sensitive than the market, below 1 less.
explain.betaMissing: Not enough index data on the same dates as the portfolio to compute this.
explain.correlation: The figure {value} is the average correlation across every pair of stocks in the portfolio. Closer to 1 means the holdings move together and diversification is less effective; closer to 0 means they are more independent.

result.exceedanceNote: The deeper the decline, the lower its probability. A point above the 50% line is more likely to occur than not.
result.lossScaleNote: The same decline levels, valued against the stocks held. Cash is excluded.
